cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a Central Asian (Turkmen-type) tribal rug/bag face with a repeating diamond-lattice "gul" motif in deep reds, browns, and dark blue, flatly photographed on a neutral background — a classic ethnographic textile with clear pile weave, borders, and design, typical of the Turkmen/Central Asian weaving tradition.

physical.physical_description:
Bag face

WARP: white and brown wool; Z-spun; 20 threads per inch (80 per dm).

WEFT: dark brown wool; Z-spun, unplied, 2 parallel threads per shoot; 2 shoots after each row of knots; 14 knots per inch (50 knots per dm).

PILE: wool; 8 colours: dark red, red, yellow, dark green, dark blue, brown, light brown, white; asymmetrical knot open to the left and tied around 2 threads; 140 knots per sq. inch (2000 per sq. dm).

SIDE FINISH: 3 cords overcast with brown wool.

END FINISH: Lower: missing.  Upper 1.5 cms. plain weave with brown weft then 1.5 cms. plain weave with white weft turned under and stitched in place with brown wool.  At the turn there are 12 blocks of 2 rows of red and blue soumak, between which there may have been loops to be used to secure the bag.

DESIGN: Field: dark red ground with 6 rows each containing 6 guls.  In the centre of each is a quartered hexagon mostly in dark red and dark blue, occasionally in dark green, with a triangle in each quarter.  The hexagon lies within a dark blue stepped cross quartered in red and white.  In the lowest band the cross is quartered alternately in red and dark blue ie. without white.  The secondary motif is offset between the guls in 5 rows of 5 and 2 half motifs.  This motif is a quartered hooked diamond in mainly dark red and dark blue, occasionally in dark green; each quarter containing a triangle.  The hooks are paired diagonally in red and mainly dark blue, occasionally dark green.  The hooks are decorated with further hooks in yellow or white.

Main border: dark blue ground with a floral meander in red and dark red decorated with white and yellow.

Inner and outer borders: diagonal blocks of ladder-like lines in all colours on a red ground.

Outer side borders: undecorated dark red.

Lower band: incomplete; three bands of floral sprigs alternating in dark green with yellow flowers and dark blue with white flower to form diagonal bands rising from the lower left.

Upper band: dark red ground decorated with part of what was probably a floral meander design.  Heat-shaped V-motifs are visible.

physical.physical_description:
Spindle bag, also known as an ok-bash; hand-knotted woollen pile on woollen warp and weft; Central Asian, Turkoman, mid-19th century.

WARP: white wool; Z2S; 21 threads per inch (85 per dm).

WEFT: dark brown wool; Z2S; 2 shoots after each row of knots;  18 knots per inch (72 per dm).

PILE: wool; 9 colours: dark red, red, light red, yellow, green, dark blue, blue, dark brown, white; symmetrical knot tied around 2 threads; 189 per sq. inch (3060 per sq.dm).

SIDE FINISH: (described as woven): left: (incomplete) 2 cords overcast in small blocks of red and green wool; right: missing.

END FINISH: (described as woven): evidence at both ends of narrow band of plainweave with white and then red wool, turned and secured by chevron overstitching in 2 blocks of red and 2 of blue for 5.5" (14 cms) from the top edge when in use.   This would have strengthened the opening.

DESIGN: (described as in use): Field: 10 complete andd 2 incomplete bands of zigzags in green, red, dark blue and dark red with a line of small crosses in each.   Along the top the last band of zigzags is filled in dark red with one of the crosses in each triangle.  Along the bottom the triangles are in green and dark blue.

Main border: (lower and upper only): white ground with a linked floral motif in reds and dark blue with a pair of tendrils to tbe right of each.
Inner and Outer borders (on each side of the main border): a band of interlocking Y-motifs which extends along both sides of the piece.   Above the top border and outside the side borders is a band of undecorated dark red.   This becomes the ground for the bottom panel, now cut into triangles.
There are 4 small dark red triangles below the bottom border, each with 3 V-shaped bands, with small crosses, in dark blue, red and green, mirroring the zigzags in the field.
The warp runs the width of the bag when in use; this piece was woven with the points on theright hand side.

Date catalogued: 11.12.96

physical.physical_description:
Bag face.

WARP: cream/light brown wool; Z2S; 17 threads per inch (70 per dm).

WEFT: brown wool; Z-spun, unplied; 2 shoots after each row of knots, one if a single thread and one is 2 parallel threads; 13 knots per inch (50 per dm).

PILE: wool; 7 colours: dark red, red, orange, green, dark blue, blue, white; asymmetrical knot open to the left and tied around 2 threads; 110 knots per sq. inch (1750 per sq. dm).

SIDE FINISH: 2 cords overcast with brown wool.

END FINISH: Lower: missing but evidence of plain weave with cream weft.  Upper: 2 cms plain weave with red weft, turned and stitched in place; webbing attached later.

DESIGN: Field: red ground with 3 bands of 3 guls of a stepped cross quartered either orange/white or orange/dark blue and outlined in dark blue with a hooked cross in the centre, either dark blue or green on a dark red hexagon.  There is a secondary motif of 2 and 2 half bands of 2 and 2 half motifs.  Small geometric motifs in the centre lie on a red diamond with a striped border and 8 projections.  The horizontal ones are hooked; the vertical ones are wide, decorated and hooked.

Main border: red ground with hooked rectangles containing a red X-motif along the top and bottom borders and with inward-facing pairs of horns between them.  Along the sides the rectangle extends into triangular-like upper and lower corners.

Inner border: red ground with small blocks of other colours alternating with white and yellow flowerheads on brown.

Outer borders: (1) red ground with green latched hooks from either side interspersed along the bottom with small white squares and blue and yellow diagonal blocks (2) red ground with diagonal blocks of dark blue, blue and green.

Outermost border: undecorated red along the sides, which becomes the ground for the upper and lower bands.

Upper band: six vertical lines each ending in a pair of horns and composed of blue or green blocks.  From each there descends 2 pairs of diagonal lines in the same colours.  In the area between the vertical lines there are groups of 6 stylised flowerheads in dark blue and green and above the horns are 2 narrow bands of diagonal blocks in red, green and dark blue and above them a single narrow band of dark blue.  There is a patch from another carpet in the top centre.

Lower band: 6 vertical stems, hooked at the top and decorated with 2 parallel lines of either dark blue or dark green blocks, each bearing 5 pairs of branches decorated with green or blue blocks.

physical.physical_description:
Saddle cover (made from something else and requires more thought)

WARP: cream wool; Z2S; 18 threads per inch (70 per dm).

WEFT: light brown wool; unable to ascertain spin and twist; 2 shoots after every row of knots; 21 knots per inch (86 per dm).

PILE: wool; 6 colours: dark red with some bleeding into the cream, red, dark blue, blue, dark brown, cream; asymmetrical knot open to the right and tied around 2 threads; 189 knots per sq. inch (3010 per sq. dm).

SIDE FINISH: Lower part: one cord oversewn with blue wool.  Upper part: kelim band with slits; not using weft from the piled areas (which is fine) but using warp wool.  Traces of a fringe.

END FINISH: Lower: maximum of 3.5 cms. of plain weave with cream weft; turned and stitched in place.  Upper: one row of blue soumak the 3.5 cms. plain weave with cream weft.

DESIGN: two equal parts joined vertically.  There is now an arch shaped with a band above it.  The arch contains a square with two rectangles and several borders - the outer one contains stepped diamonds and the inner ones are checked.  The band has a central hexagon with half a hexagon to either side; these contain a diamond motif.  There is an "insert" in the sixth border from either side - there might originally have been a slit here.

Date catalogued: 21.6.94
